stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the graphs of \(y = 2x\) and \(y = -x + 9\) intersect at point \(P\). The two lines and the \(x\)-axis form a triangle. What is the area of this triangle?
solution: The lines meet the \(x\)-axis at \((0, 0)\) and \((9, 0)\), so the base of the triangle is 9 and its height is the \(y\)-coordinate of \(P\), 6.
verify:
x, y = symbols('x y')
P = solve([y - 2*x, y + x - 9], [x, y])
assert P == {x: 3, y: 6}
a, b = solve(2*x, x)[0], solve(-x + 9, x)[0]
area = Rational(1, 2)*abs(b - a)*P[y]
assert area == 27
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [area]
